claims.text: The POL-NS-07 anti-farming check trips on the driver's own profile, and it trips on both limbs. driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 7, which is 4 or more, and 7 divided by driver_profile.completed_trips_30d of 61 is 0.115, comfortably above the 0.08 threshold. Both of these are fields POL-GEN-01 permits to be cited, and only for this test. The consequence under POL-NS-07 is that the driver's compensation is WITHHELD and the matter escalates - it does not turn on anything about the rider.

Because the POL-NS-07 check trips, POL-NS-09(d) makes escalation to a human reviewer mandatory, and escalation under POL-NS-09 is terminal for the automated pipeline: no monetary ruling issues and the disputed SGD 4.00 is placed on hold rather than collected or refunded. The payments ledger already shows exactly that state - payment_status PENDING with refund_issued_sgd 0.00 - so the rider is not left carrying the disputed charge while the review is open.

POL-NS-07 does not merely escalate; it requires the escalation packet to DIRECT the reviewer to refund the rider's cancellation fee in full, so that the rider does not fund a dispute the platform has not resolved. The refund the rider asks for is therefore the destination the packet must carry once the reviewer opens it, not an open question for the reviewer to work out from scratch.

The escalation is driven entirely by the driver's 30-day termination pattern, not by any abuse on the rider's side. rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 1, below the 3 that POL-NS-09(d) reads, and rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 0, so POL-NS-09(c) is not engaged. Because escalation REPLACES the monetary outcome, the automated pipeline does not collect the fee from this rider.

claims.text: All four limbs of POL-NS-01 hold on this trip. (a) The trip record carries a driver arrival event at 06:41:20. (b) The trace places the driver inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius from 06:41:10, ten seconds before that marker. (c) The driver then held position inside the geofence continuously for 507 seconds against the 300 second STANDARD minimum, the dwell running from the first qualifying in-geofence fix as the clause requires and not from the arrival event. (d) The trip was terminated by the driver at 06:49:37 under cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, well after the required dwell elapsed at 06:46:10. The cancellation fee is legitimately chargeable at the SGD 4.00 fixed by the fee schedule's greater-of rule for a STANDARD pickup in a RYDE_X vehicle.

The POL-NS-02 proximity test is satisfied with room to spare, so POL-NS-01 limb (b) is unassailable. Fifty-two of the driver's fixes are qualifying in-radius fixes inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, and the qualifying run opens at 06:41:10, before the recorded arrival event. The rider cannot argue the driver never arrived at the pin; the fixes say he did.

There is no waiting-period shortfall for the rider to exploit under POL-NS-06. The effective in-geofence dwell is 507 seconds against the 300 second STANDARD minimum — a surplus of 207 seconds — so the refund-on-shortfall rule never engages. Nor is any traffic advisory needed, because the qualifying hold is a single unbroken run and POL-NS-06(i) accumulation only matters where there are separate intervals to add together. That EV-ADVIS-00207-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) therefore costs the driver nothing: absence of an advisory is citable but irrelevant where the dwell is already sufficient on its own.

The arrival marker is not false under POL-NS-05. At the moment the driver marked arrival his fixes are inside the geofence and stationary — the qualifying run of 52 fixes begins at 06:41:10 and the driver holds position from there — so he was neither more than 300 m from the pin nor travelling at 15 km/h or above when he marked arrival. The recomputation POL-NS-05 performs on a false marker is not required here, and the marker stands as a true one.

POL-NS-04 cannot run on this record. Its limb (a) requires at least one locating or coordinating message sent by the rider during the waiting window, and the chat log holds four entries across 06:41:21 to 06:49:20 — one system 'Your driver has arrived' notice and three messages from the driver — with the rider sending nothing at all. With limb (a) failing, the rider-exoneration clause is out, and the driver's reply conduct under limb (b) is never reached.

The rider's own device track refutes the claim that he came down. Across 118 rider fixes in the window his position sits between 1,894 and 1,907 metres from the pickup pin, never once inside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius; his qualifying presence fix count is zero. The rider was not at or near the pickup point at any time during the wait, and his assertion that he was 'a few minutes late' to the kerb is contradicted by the geometry computed from his own device.

Wrong-entrance allocation under POL-NS-03 does not arise. That clause is confined to a driver stationary outside the arrival radius but within 400 m of the pin; here the driver's stationary qualifying fixes are inside the 50 m arrival radius itself. There is no mislocation to apportion between the parties and no pin-ambiguity goodwill to pay out of platform funds.

The driver behaved exactly as the policy expects of a driver kept waiting. He placed an in-app call at 06:45:10 that went unanswered, and sent three in-app messages at 06:42:30, 06:46:02 and 06:49:20 — each delivered and each read by the rider — before cancelling at 06:49:37. This was a patient, documented, eight-and-a-half-minute wait at the correct block, not the speculative cancellation the rider's claim implies.

On a verified rider no-show the driver's compensation is fixed by POL-NS-07 at 80 percent of the itemised fee — SGD 3.20 of the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee. The fare breakdown's cancellation_fee of 4.00 reconciles with the STANDARD zone-class fee of 4.00 and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee of 4.00 under the fee schedule's greater-of rule, so no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect arises and the fee line needs no discount.

I do not dispute the arithmetic the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check turns on, and I will not substitute the lifetime prior_no_show_flags counter for it. driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 7, which is 4 or more, and 7 divided by completed_trips_30d of 61 is 11.5 percent, above the 0.08 threshold; both limbs are met, so that clause withholds compensation and sends this case to escalation under POL-NS-09, which is terminal and holds the disputed fee rather than collecting or refunding it. I cannot argue that counter away, and I do not try to. I ask only that the Judge read it for what it is: a trailing-30-day pattern on the driver's profile, which POL-GEN-01 permits to be cited for this test and no other, and not a fact about what happened at Blk 682 on this trip — where the trip's own telemetry shows a genuine, documented no-show by a rider who was 1.9 km away.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: on the merits of the trip itself the driver is right, but the fee cannot be collected and no compensation can be paid, so this case goes to a human reviewer.

The driver waited long enough at the correct place. The GPS trace EV-GPS-00207 (weight 1.0) places his vehicle inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius from 06:41:10 and holding position without a break for 507 seconds - a surplus of 207 seconds over the 300 second STANDARD minimum - and the trip record EV-TRIP-00207 (weight 1.0) shows the arrival event at 06:41:20, no boarding event, and termination by the driver at 06:49:37 under cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, well after the required dwell elapsed at 06:46:10. All four limbs of POL-NS-01 therefore hold and the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee is legitimately chargeable. The supporting clauses raise nothing against it: POL-NS-02 is satisfied by the 52 qualifying in-radius fixes; POL-NS-05 finds no false arrival marker because the driver was inside the geofence and stationary at the marker; POL-NS-06 finds no shortfall, and the MISSING advisory EV-ADVIS-00207-01 (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) costs nothing because the hold is a single unbroken run needing no accumulation; POL-NS-03 never engages because the driver was inside the arrival radius, not outside it; and POL-NS-04 cannot run because its limb (a) requires a locating message from the rider, and the rider sent nothing - the four chat entries are one system notice and three driver messages (06:42:30, 06:46:02, 06:49:20), all delivered and all read. The rider's own device track sits between 1,894 and 1,907 m from the pin across the whole window, so the account of having come down 'a few minutes late' is contradicted by the geometry from his own phone.

What stops the money is POL-NS-07. Its anti-farming check reads driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d = 7, which is 4 or more, and 7 divided by driver_profile.completed_trips_30d of 61 = 11.5 percent, above the 0.08 threshold. Both limbs are met, so the driver's compensation of SGD 3.20 (80 percent of the SGD 4.00 fee) is WITHHELD and POL-NS-09(d) makes escalation to a human reviewer mandatory. Escalation is terminal for the automated pipeline: no refund and no payment issue now, and the disputed SGD 4.00 is held rather than collected from the rider or refunded - the ledger already shows payment_status PENDING with refund_issued_sgd 0.00.

The escalation packet carries one instruction that POL-NS-07 itself requires: direct the reviewer to refund the rider's cancellation fee in full, so that the rider does not fund a dispute the platform has not resolved. The open question the reviewer must settle is the driver's trailing-30-day no-show termination pattern, not the events at Blk 682 on 29 July. The rider's own counters are clean - no_show_disputes_30d = 1, below the 3 that POL-NS-09(d) reads, and disputes_with_counterparty_90d = 0, so POL-NS-09(c) is not engaged - and no rider-side abuse is in issue. The lifetime prior_no_show_flags counter was raised in argument only to be set aside; it is context only under POL-GEN-01 and is read for no test here.
referrals: POL-NS-07: direct the human reviewer to refund the rider's cancellation fee of SGD 4.00 in full; the disputed fee remains held rather than collected or refunded by the automated pipeline while review is pending.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: the charge was correctly raised, but this case does not end in a payment to either of you — it goes to a human reviewer, and the SGD 4.00 stays on hold.

What the record shows. The trip record (EV-TRIP-00207, weight 1.0) carries a driver arrival tap at 06:41:20. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-00207, weight 1.0) places the vehicle inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius from 06:41:10 and holding station continuously for 507 seconds against the 300 second STANDARD minimum, and the driver cancelled at 06:49:37 under RIDER_NO_SHOW, well after the required dwell elapsed at 06:46:10. All four limbs of POL-NS-01 therefore hold, and the fee is legitimately chargeable at SGD 4.00 — the greater of the STANDARD zone-class fee (4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (4.00) under the fee schedule's greater-of rule, which reconciles with fare_breakdown.cancellation_fee of 4.00, so no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect arises. POL-NS-02 is satisfied (52 qualifying in-radius fixes), POL-NS-05 shows the arrival marker was true (in-geofence and stationary when tapped), POL-NS-06 shows no shortfall, and POL-NS-03 does not apply because the driver was inside the arrival radius rather than outside it.

The rider's account is not supported. Your own device track (EV-GPS-00207) puts you between 1,894 m and 1,907 m from the pickup pin for the whole wait, with zero qualifying fixes inside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius. POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate you because its limb (a) fails: the chat log (EV-CHAT-00207, weight 1.0) holds four messages — one system notice and three from the driver — and you sent none. The MISSING traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-00207-01, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) is properly disclosed and is irrelevant here: the hold was a single unbroken qualifying run, so POL-NS-06(i) accumulation never comes into play.

Why no money issues. POL-NS-07 pays the driver only after an anti-farming check, and that check trips on the driver's own profile (EV-DPROF-00207, weight 1.0): no_show_terminations_30d is 7 (4 or more) and 7 / 61 completed_trips_30d is 11.5%, above the 0.08 threshold. Both limbs are met. POL-GEN-01 allows those two fields to be cited for this test and no other; they are a trailing-window pattern on the profile, not a fact about what happened at Blk 682. The clause consequence is fixed: the driver's SGD 3.20 (80% of SGD 4.00) is withheld and the case escalates under POL-NS-09(d), which is terminal — I issue no monetary outcome, and the disputed SGD 4.00 remains in the state the ledger already shows (payment_status PENDING, refund_issued_sgd 0.00), neither collected nor refunded.

This escalation is not a finding against the rider. rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 1, below the 3 that limb reads, and disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 0 on both sides, so POL-NS-09(c) is not engaged; the trigger is solely the driver's 30-day termination pattern. The driver's own concession to the same effect is accepted.

Confidence and integrity. No artifact meets the POL-NS-08(a)–(d) impairment limbs (no clock skew beyond 90 s, complete 10 s telemetry with no gaps and the rider track present, chat message count matches the trip record, fare line reconciles), and every artifact carrying a deciding fact has weight_multiplier 1.0, so the confidence cap under POL-GEN-02(2) is 1.0; my confidence is 0.9. The bundle mean is context only and is not the cap.

The packet carries two things the reviewer must act on: the POL-NS-07 direction to refund your SGD 4.00 cancellation fee in full, and the open question whether the driver's trailing-30-day anti-farming pattern is genuine before that refund is processed.
referrals: POL-NS-07 — the escalation packet must DIRECT the human reviewer to refund the rider's cancellation fee of SGD 4.00 in full. The POL-NS-07 anti-farming check trips on driver_profile (no_show_terminations_30d 7, which is >= 4, and 7 / completed_trips_30d 61 = 11.5%, above 0.08); compensation of SGD 3.20 is withheld and the packet must carry the full-refund direction so the rider does not fund an unresolved dispute.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties should read this the same way: the record of what happened at Blk 682 Woodlands Ave 6 on 29 July 2026 is clear, but the policy does not let the automated pipeline finish the case.

WHAT THE RECORD SHOWS. The trip record (EV-TRIP-00207) has the driver arriving at 06:41:20 and terminating at 06:49:37 as RIDER_NO_SHOW. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-00207) puts him inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius from 06:41:10 and holding still for 507 seconds — 8 min 27 s — against the 300-second minimum, starting from the first qualifying in-geofence fix as POL-NS-01 requires. All four POL-NS-01 conditions therefore hold, and the SGD 4.00 fee is validly chargeable under the fee schedule's greater-of rule (STANDARD zone fee SGD 4.00, RYDE_X tier fee SGD 4.00). The rider's assertion that he came down only a few minutes late is rejected: his own device track in the same trace (118 fixes) sits 1,894–1,907 m from the pin across the whole waiting window, never inside the 100 m rider-presence radius, with zero qualifying presence fixes. POL-NS-04 (rider contact unanswered) cannot apply because the rider sent no locating message; POL-NS-05 (false arrival marker) cannot apply because the driver was stationary inside the geofence at the marker; POL-NS-03 (wrong entrance) cannot apply because he was inside the arrival radius, not stationary 50–400 m outside it. The missing traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00207-01 (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) is citable but changes nothing: the 507-second hold was a single unbroken run, so POL-NS-06 accumulation never arises and no refund-on-shortfall is available. None of the POL-NS-08(a)–(d) impairments is met (clock agreement within 90 s, no trace gap, 4 chat entries matching the recorded chat count, the SGD 4.00 line reconciling), so no POL-NS-08 escalation applies.

WHY THE CASE STILL GOES TO A HUMAN. POL-NS-07 would pay the driver 80% of the fee (SGD 3.20) only if its anti-farming check passes. It does not. driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 7 (4 or more) and 7 ÷ 61 completed trips is 11.5%, above the 0.08 threshold; both limbs are met, so compensation is WITHHELD and POL-NS-09(d) makes escalation to a human reviewer mandatory. Escalation is terminal: no money moves, and the SGD 4.00 remains held rather than collected or refunded (the fare record already shows payment_status PENDING and refund_issued_sgd 0.00) while review is pending. The rider's no_show_disputes_30d is 1, below the 3 POL-NS-09(d) reads, and disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 0 for both parties, so no rider-side abuse limb or POL-NS-09(c) conflict is engaged; the escalation rests entirely on the driver's trailing-30-day pattern. That counter is citable for this test only and is not a finding about this trip. The driver's passing reference to the lifetime prior_no_show_flags counter was flagged as a context-only field under POL-GEN-01 and was not used as a ground of decision by either side.

THE OPEN QUESTION AND THE INSTRUCTION THAT RIDES WITH IT. The reviewer must confirm the anti-farming pattern and complete the disposition of the held SGD 4.00. POL-NS-07 directs that the escalation packet instruct the reviewer to refund the rider's SGD 4.00 cancellation fee in full, so that the rider does not fund a dispute the platform has not resolved. Confidence is above the 0.70 floor; the deciding facts rest on artifacts of weight 1.0.
referrals: POL-NS-07: Direct the human reviewer to refund the rider's cancellation fee of SGD 4.00 in full, so that the rider does not fund a dispute the platform has not resolved.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and to the driver.

On the merits of the no-show, the driver is right and the rider's claim fails. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-00207, weight 1.0, 100% coverage, no gaps) shows the driver inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius at Blk 682 Woodlands Ave 6 from 06:41:10, stationary, for one unbroken in-geofence run of 507 seconds, with 52 qualifying in-radius fixes. That is 207 seconds more than the 300-second STANDARD minimum dwell. The trip record (EV-TRIP-00207, weight 1.0) records the arrival marker at 06:41:20 — ten seconds after the first qualifying fix — and records the driver cancelling at 06:49:37 under cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, which is after the dwell elapsed at 06:46:10. All four limbs of POL-NS-01 hold: (a) an arrival event, (b) in-geofence fixes before it, (c) a continuous qualifying dwell of 507 s against 300 s, (d) no boarding and a driver termination on RIDER_NO_SHOW after the dwell. The SGD 4.00 fee reconciles with the fee schedule's greater-of rule (STANDARD zone-class fee 4.00; RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee 4.00 — it is a tie and the higher figure governs), so no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect arises.

Three clauses that could have displaced that result do not. POL-NS-05 does not catch the arrival marker: at 06:41:20 the driver was inside the geofence and stationary, not more than 300 m from the pin and not travelling at 15 km/h or above, so no recomputation of the waiting clock is required. POL-NS-06 produces no shortfall (507 s against 300 s), and because the hold was a single unbroken run, the POL-NS-06(i) accumulation rule was never needed — so the absence of a traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-00207-01, MISSING, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) is citable but does not change anything; the driver's point on this is accepted. POL-NS-03 is confined to a driver stationary outside the arrival radius but within 400 m of the pin; here the stationary fixes are inside the 50 m radius itself, so there is no mislocation to apportion and no pin-ambiguity goodwill.

The rider's account is contradicted by his own device. The rider track in EV-GPS-00207 places him between 1,894 m and 1,907 m from the pickup pin across 118 fixes, never once within the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius, with zero qualifying presence fixes. The chat log (EV-CHAT-00207, weight 1.0) holds four entries between 06:41:21 and 06:49:20 — one system arrival notice and three messages from the driver, each delivered and each read — and nothing at all from the rider. Limb (a) of POL-NS-04 (a locating or coordinating message from the rider) therefore fails, so that exoneration clause cannot run. The driver's conduct was patient and documented: an unanswered in-app call at 06:45:10 and messages at 06:42:30, 06:46:02 and 06:49:20, before cancelling at 06:49:37.

What prevents a ruling in the driver's favour is POL-NS-07's anti-farming check, and both sides accept the arithmetic of it. The driver profile (EV-DPROF-00207, weight 1.0) records 7 no-show terminations in the trailing 30 days against 61 completed trips — at or above 4 terminations, and 11.5%, above the 0.08 threshold. Both limbs are met. The consequence is fixed by the clause: the driver's compensation of SGD 3.20 (80% of the SGD 4.00 fee) is withheld, and the case escalates under POL-NS-09(d). Those two profile fields are citable under POL-GEN-01 for this test only; the lifetime prior_no_show_flags counter was mentioned but expressly not used, and it is not a ground of this decision. No rider-side escalation ground is engaged either: rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 1, below the 3 that POL-NS-09(d) reads, and neither party's disputes_with_counterparty_90d reaches 2 under POL-NS-09(c).

ESCALATE is terminal for the automated pipeline, so no money moves here: amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd are both null, and the disputed SGD 4.00 stays held rather than collected or refunded. The payments ledger already shows that state (payment_status PENDING, refund_issued_sgd 0.00, total_charged 4.50 including the platform fee 0.50). The escalation trigger is the tripped POL-NS-07 anti-farming check under POL-NS-09(d). The open question the human reviewer must settle is the anti-farming review of driver DRV-01948's trailing-30-day termination pattern and any account-level action it warrants. The refund itself is not an open question: under POL-NS-07 the escalation packet directs the reviewer to refund the rider's SGD 4.00 cancellation fee in full, and that reference is carried in referrals.
referrals: POL-NS-07: direct the human reviewer to refund the rider's SGD 4.00 cancellation fee in full, so that the rider does not fund a dispute the platform has not resolved.

ledger.claim: The POL-NS-07 anti-farming check trips on the driver's own profile, and it trips on both limbs. driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 7, which is 4 or more, and 7 divided by driver_profile.completed_trips_30d of 61 is 0.115, comfortably above the 0.08 threshold. Both of these are fields POL-GEN-01 permits to be cited, and only for this test. The consequence under POL-NS-07 is that the driver's compensation is WITHHELD and the matter escalates - it does not turn on anything about the rider.

Because the POL-NS-07 check trips, POL-NS-09(d) makes escalation to a human reviewer mandatory, and escalation under POL-NS-09 is terminal for the automated pipeline: no monetary ruling issues and the disputed SGD 4.00 is placed on hold rather than collected or refunded. The payments ledger already shows exactly that state - payment_status PENDING with refund_issued_sgd 0.00 - so the rider is not left carrying the disputed charge while the review is open.

POL-NS-07 does not merely escalate; it requires the escalation packet to DIRECT the reviewer to refund the rider's cancellation fee in full, so that the rider does not fund a dispute the platform has not resolved. The refund the rider asks for is therefore the destination the packet must carry once the reviewer opens it, not an open question for the reviewer to work out from scratch.

The escalation is driven entirely by the driver's 30-day termination pattern, not by any abuse on the rider's side. rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 1, below the 3 that POL-NS-09(d) reads, and rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 0, so POL-NS-09(c) is not engaged. Because escalation REPLACES the monetary outcome, the automated pipeline does not collect the fee from this rider.

All four limbs of POL-NS-01 hold on this trip. (a) The trip record carries a driver arrival event at 06:41:20. (b) The trace places the driver inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius from 06:41:10, ten seconds before that marker. (c) The driver then held position inside the geofence continuously for 507 seconds against the 300 second STANDARD minimum, the dwell running from the first qualifying in-geofence fix as the clause requires and not from the arrival event. The POL-NS-02 proximity test is satisfied with room to spare, so POL-NS-01 limb (b) is unassailable. Fifty-two of the driver's fixes are qualifying in-radius fixes inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, and the qualifying run opens at 06:41:10, before the recorded arrival event. The rider cannot argue the driver never arrived at the pin; the fixes say he did.

There is no waiting-period shortfall for the rider to exploit under POL-NS-06. The effective in-geofence dwell is 507 seconds against the 300 second STANDARD minimum — a surplus of 207 seconds — so the refund-on-shortfall rule never engages. Nor is any traffic advisory needed, because the qualifying hold is a single unbroken run and POL-NS-06(i) accumulation only matters where there are separate intervals to add together. That EV-ADVIS-00207-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) therefore costs the driver nothing: absence of an advisory is citable but irrelevant where the dwell is already sufficient on its own.

The arrival marker is not false under POL-NS-05. At the moment the driver marked arrival his fixes are inside the geofence and stationary — the qualifying run of 52 fixes begins at 06:41:10 and the driver holds position from there — so he was neither more than 300 m from the pin nor travelling at 15 km/h or above when he marked arrival. The recomputation POL-NS-05 performs on a false marker is not required here, and the marker stands as a true one.

POL-NS-04 cannot run on this record. Its limb (a) requires at least one locating or coordinating message sent by the rider during the waiting window, and the chat log holds four entries across 06:41:21 to 06:49:20 — one system 'Your driver has arrived' notice and three messages from the driver — with the rider sending nothing at all. With limb (a) failing, the rider-exoneration clause is out, and the driver's reply conduct under limb (b) is never reached.

The rider's own device track refutes the claim that he came down. Across 118 rider fixes in the window his position sits between 1,894 and 1,907 metres from the pickup pin, never once inside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius; his qualifying presence fix count is zero. The rider was not at or near the pickup point at any time during the wait, and his assertion that he was 'a few minutes late' to the kerb is contradicted by the geometry computed from his own device.

Wrong-entrance allocation under POL-NS-03 does not arise. That clause is confined to a driver stationary outside the arrival radius but within 400 m of the pin; here the driver's stationary qualifying fixes are inside the 50 m arrival radius itself. There is no mislocation to apportion between the parties and no pin-ambiguity goodwill to pay out of platform funds.

He placed an in-app call at 06:45:10 that went unanswered, and sent three in-app messages at 06:42:30, 06:46:02 and 06:49:20 — each delivered and each read by the rider — before cancelling at 06:49:37.
